topic.title: You are the unpaid cast of the song
topic.claim: A song gets a hookstep before the film exists, and the Reel you make is the ad.
topic.behaviour: 'Tu Mil Jaaye' from King was released 2 November and passed 100 million combined views and plays on YouTube. It reportedly has 283,000 Reels creations, and fans are recreating the hookstep at celebrations. The figures are promotional and not independently verified. King itself releases on 24 December 2026.
topic.mechanism: A song with an easy step is built to be copied. Each copy is a free ad shown to friends who trust you more than a poster, and the film is still a month away.
topic.group: Instagram users who post Reels and attend parties
topic.moment: You shoot the hookstep at a cousin's sangeet because everyone else did, and nobody asks whether you liked the song.

turn.believed: A song goes viral because people love it.
turn.actually: Some songs are made for the Reel: an easy step, a clean hook. The loved version and the shared version are not always the same.

topic.villain: a promotion model that turns every viewer into a distribution channel
topic.because: The film gets reach from the audience for free. The audience gets a moment to post.

proof.fact: The song was released 2 November and passed 100 million combined views and plays on YouTube; there are 283,000 reported Instagram Reels creations; the figures are promotional and not independently verified; King releases on 24 December 2026.

topic.payoff: If you can do the step in five seconds, someone designed it that way.
topic.send_to: The friend who posts every trending audio.
real_details: DJs are adding it to party playlists.
topic.news_peg: 'Tu Mil Jaaye' from King crossed 100 million plays, reported 2026-11-19
topic.why_now: Wedding season is starting and the hookstep is about to be everywhere.

score.why: The hookstep at the sangeet shows the viewer is the film's ad channel, said dryly; the source figures are used only lightly.
